title: Graph bandwidth

problem.name: Graph bandwidth
problem.statement_latex:
For $G=(V,E)$ with $n$ vertices, compute
\[\operatorname{bw}(G)=\min_{\pi:V\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}[n]}\max_{uv\in E}|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|.\]
Bandwidth minimizes the largest separation of adjacent vertices, equivalently the bandwidth of a symmetrically permuted adjacency matrix.
The quantum bound counts QRAM time and the classical bound counts RAM operations on the explicit graph.

quantum.details_latex: A decomposition into constrained vertex-ordering instances permits variable-time quantum search and partial subset preprocessing. The quoted time includes the search over decomposition choices and assumes coherent access to stored dynamic-programming values. Polynomial factors include graph processing and the objective threshold.

classical.details_latex: The algorithm uses structural restrictions on feasible layouts to reduce the search space. The quantum construction also accelerates a simpler $O^*(5^n)$ formulation, while the $4.383^n$ bound supplies the stronger overall classical comparison. Both bounds use the number of vertices as their exponential parameter.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup from $4.383^n$ to $2.946^n$; quantum minimum finding and variable-time amplitude amplification are the principal acceleration tools.

evidence.description_latex: The upper bound is rigorous in the stated memory model. The best-algorithm comparison has partial evidence from the established classical exact-algorithm literature.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomial active subset, layout and objective registers require exponential QRAM for preprocessing. The nested searches and stored table make useful large instances a fault-tolerant target.
